summary: The Couch Investor (published 2026-09-18) reacts to the Fed's first rate hike since 2023 — a unanimous 25bp increase — and argues the market is overreacting, noting the S&P 500 sits just 3.5% off all-time highs and Nasdaq 100 about 5.7% down. He walks through the Fed's reasoning: underlying inflation not returning to 2% fast enough, a strong labor market (4.1% unemployment) giving room to tighten, and Middle East tensions feeding inflation. The dot plot shows 16 of 18 participants expecting at least one more 2026 hike and none seeing 2027 cuts; GDP forecasts were raised slightly (2.3% for 2026, 2.4% for 2027). His advice: don't panic over 25bp in a healthy economy — these moments are gifts for long-term investors, as the 5% 10-year yield scare of 2023 proved. If the market pulls back harder, he's conditional-buying on weakness: Google at $300, Meta under $600, Amazon at/near $200, Nvidia at/under $200, Nebius (NBIS) way under $200 (maybe $150–160 long-term), and Micron back around $700. On 'do nothing': SoFi is back under $17 and a good business he's super bullish on, but has zero momentum and macro overhang — better to wait until sentiment flips; same for ServiceNow.
